tob-0176: Pistis Sophia is the greatest Gnostic gospel to survive — a talk in which the risen Jesus schools his followers in the hidden frame of the heavens. tob-4276: William Prescott’s History of the Conquest of Mexico is the classic English telling of Cortés’s casting-down of the Aztec realm. Blind through much of his labor, Prescott wrought from Spanish archives a tale of high drama. This first volume spans the groundwork and the landing at Veracruz.
tob-4146-15476: Volume three of Ganguli’s Mahabharata brings the epic to the war’s edge — the hosts arrayed at Kurukshetra and the Bhagavad Gita sounding its word. The volume holds some of the poem’s best-loved turns. Ganguli’s hand keeps their stateliness and sweep.
tob-9052-15476: Volume three brings Ganguli’s Mahabharata to the war’s edge — the hosts mustered at Kurukshetra and Krishna’s great word, the Bhagavad Gita, unfolding. tob-13329-15476: Volume three brings the Mahabharata to battle’s brink — hosts arrayed at Kurukshetra, the Bhagavad Gita’s teaching ringing out. The epic’s dearest passages throng this volume, from Krishna’s showing-forth to Arjuna’s resolve. Ganguli’s hand keeps their stateliness and sweep.
tob-0076: Edmund Whittaker’s huge history trails physics from the old aether to Maxwell and Einstein — the teachings on light, shock-power, and lodestone-force across two thousand years. Penned by a great mathematician, it is the classic account of old physics’ rise. The book stays needful for science historians.
tob-4176: St. Teresa’s Inner Castle charts the soul’s inward fare through seven dwelling-places to oneness with God — the crown-book of Carmelite holy-mystery. Zimmerman’s Englishing bore her shining Spanish to our readers. The book stays the great handbook of still prayer.
tob-9776: Maas’s Catholic wordbook piece on the Six-Days treats the world’s making — the Church’s word on Genesis’ first leaf. His learned muster spans father-lore and new reading alike. It weighs the fathers’ readings against latter-day science. The piece stays a clear setting-forth of olden Catholic writ-reading.
cia-0000102976: An August 1983 report detailing a labor camp for young offenders near Irkutsk in Siberia. Juvenile prisoners were put to work in the same forced-labor tradition as adult camps, in one of the harshest climates on earth. The document is a reminder that the Soviet camp system reached even children, and that the CIA documented it camp by camp.
cia-0000106276: A September 1965 report on communist activity in the Laos panhandle, the narrow southern strip bordering Vietnam. This was Ho Chi Minh Trail country, where North Vietnamese forces moved men and supplies toward South Vietnam. The document is part of the CIA's long effort to map an enemy supply route that American bombs never managed to close.
cia-0000107976: An April 1967 report on Japan's economic role in developing a free Asia. Japanese investment and aid were knitting Southeast Asia into an anti-communist economic bloc. The document captures the strategy of fighting communism with factories and trade — Japan as America's economic engine in the Cold War Pacific.
cia-0000108476: The weekly terrorism situation report for August 20, 1980. By that summer, American officials were living through the Iran hostage crisis, and every week's incidents were read against that ordeal. The document preserves the drumbeat of threats that formed the background noise of the Carter presidency's final months.
cia-0000111776: A March 1985 report, its first subject blanked out, on the use of forced labor on the Soviet Siberian gas pipeline. The pipeline to Western Europe was the USSR's biggest cash earner — and, evidence suggested, built partly by prisoners. The censored first topic leaves readers wondering what else the cable contained.
cia-0000119676: An estimated February 1969 document on a U.S. Marine's desertion, told through a letter explaining his action. Personal letters became intelligence when they crossed into enemy hands — or were found. The entry is the war's human wreckage, filed as a document.
cia-0000124276: A January 1958 list, prepared for the International Geophysical Year, of Soviet stations for visually observing artificial satellites — with their geographic coordinates. Moscow published the station list openly; the CIA filed it carefully. The document is open-source intelligence at its purest: the enemy's own data, repurposed.
cia-0000126876: An August 1968 survey of world communist reaction to the invasion of Czechoslovakia. Parties from Paris to Tokyo had to choose: defend Moscow or defend Prague. The document maps the fracture — the invasion that broke the communist world's faith in itself.
cia-0000126976: An October 1975 weekly summary on Angola after independence — the companion to the weekly review, two days apart. Summaries and reviews sliced the same crisis for different readers. The document is the Angola story retold: the war after the celebration.
cia-0000132276: Situation Report 582 on the Soviet peace plan — the truncated title suggests the details. Moscow's initiative was the final diplomatic gambit before the ground war. The document examines the plan: its terms, its chances, and its failure.
cia-0000134276: A 1959 report: Caribbean tensions continuing. The basin stayed unsettled. The document is the persistence: the tensions, unabated.
cia-0000136276: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting the need for consolidation-phase policy plans — the truncated title cuts off the alternatives. Victory was assumed; the aftermath needed planning. The document is the foresight: the consolidation, planned.
cia-0000138976: A 1946 military information report on Russian activities. The watching brief. The document is the watch: the activities, noted.
cia-0000139476: A 1986 DECI hostage location task force report — the archive's spelling varies. The hunt, renamed. The document is the report: the search, continued.

cia-0000132776: A 1960 CIA file on Cuba and the Caribbean, numbered 0000132776. The island in its neighborhood. The document is the neighborhood: the region, framed.
cia-0000135676: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135676. The pre-invasion papers. The entry is the prelude: the brigade, forming.

cia-0000136776: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136776. The Bay of Pigs brigade's own documents. The entry is the brigade's: the papers, Spanish.
un-sc-res-176: Security Council Resolution 176, adopted in 1962 — aligned. The early-sixties Council at work. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.

frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d276: A memorandum of conversation, November 26, 1943 — Document 276. The day's second memcon. The memo is the second: the conversation, again.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d376: Bohlen minutes, December 1, 1943 — Document 376. December's first minuting. The minutes are December's: Bohlen, recording.
the-principal-navigations-voyages-traffi: Another volume of Hakluyt's great collection — more voyages, more discoveries, more Elizabethan daring on the high seas. The English nation's sea story continues in all its glory. Essential for all lovers of exploration and adventure. No library of English adventure is complete without Hakluyt.
arxiv-2605-09076: When AI agents collaborate, one traitor can poison the group — the Byzantine generals problem, now with language models. Haejoon Lee, Vincent-Daniel Yun, Hyeonho Oh, and Dimitra Panagou study multi-agent LLM systems that stay robust under Byzantine faults. The 2026 paper is distributed-systems security for AI teams.
arxiv-2605-09176: Training language models means crossing the valley of optimizer choices, starting from the ubiquitous AdamW. Aditya Ranganath navigates from AdamW toward memory-efficient and matrix-based optimizers. The 2026 paper is a practical field guide to training optimizers for big models.
arxiv-2605-09276: Spiking transformers — brain-inspired, event-driven — need to know which tokens matter, with honest uncertainty. Wenxuan Liu, Zecheng Hao, Tong Bu, and colleagues estimate token importance with uncertainty awareness. The 2026 paper is efficient AI that knows what it does not know.
arxiv-2605-09376: Self-driving planners love the bicycle model — simple, fast — but reality mismatches the model. Lingxue Lyu and Zihui Liu tighten constraints adaptively, aware of the mismatch, for trajectory optimization. The 2026 paper keeps planned paths safe when the model lies a little.
arxiv-2605-09476: Simplifying text across languages needs sentence-aligned corpora — complex and simple versions matched up sentence by sentence — which barely exist anywhere. This 2026 paper builds high-quality ones: Align and Shine. It is data infrastructure for multilingual text simplification at scale.
arxiv-2605-09576: Harmonic maps minimize energy between geometric spaces, and the extremal ones that stay conformal at a point form a distinguished class. Franc Forstnerič and David Kalaj solve an extremal problem for these maps. The 2026 paper is geometric analysis on energy-minimizing maps with a conformal constraint.
arxiv-2605-09776: Float a convex polytope in water — the flotation surface where it balances, and the buoyancy surface beneath it, are unique. S. Dann, O. Herscovici, and S. Myroshnychenko prove this uniqueness. The 2026 paper is delightful convex geometry, literally and wonderfully buoyant.
arxiv-2605-09876: Neptune's mean motion resonances trap Kuiper belt objects in rhythmic gravitational dances; estimating their capture ability numerically maps the outer solar system's architecture. Hailiang Li, Li-Yong Zhou, and Xiaoping Zhang perform the estimation. The 2026 paper is celestial mechanics on resonance capture.
plos-pone-0003376: Geneticists got a cheaper mapping shortcut in this 2008 methods paper. By cutting DNA at specific sites and sequencing just the adjacent fragments, called RAD markers, they found single-letter DNA differences (SNPs) and placed them on genetic maps at high density. The platform is simple and inexpensive, opening genome mapping to species with few existing genetic resources.
plos-pone-0003476: Cancer biologists found a brake on a notorious cancer gene in this 2008 paper. The Ras oncogene drives tumors partly by neutralizing p27 Kip1, a protein that restrains cell division, and the team showed the transcription factor Stat1 is essential to that shutdown. How Stat1 is phosphorylated determines whether Ras can turn cancerous, naming a lever in tumor formation.
plos-pone-0003576: Clinicians built a faster fingerprint for a killer in this 2008 paper. Identifying which pneumococcal strain causes meningitis usually requires growing the bacteria, impossible when cultures come back negative. Their sequential multiplex PCR named the serotype straight from patient samples, a tool that matters most where lab resources are thinnest.
plos-pone-0003676: In 2008, Ben-Shachar and Karry mapped faulty power plants across mental illness. Mitochondrial complex I, the cell's energy front door, showed damage in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depression, but in different brain patterns for each. The distinct maps suggest the three disorders break energy metabolism in their own ways.
plos-pone-0003776: Kalaitzidis and Neel read blood stem cells' instant reactions in this 2008 paper. Their flow-cytometry method tracked protein phosphorylation in single hematopoietic stem cells over time and across stimuli. The technique reveals how the blood system's root cells answer different calls.
plos-pone-0003876: A 2009 study found thin air keeping insects small. Klok and Harrison showed atmospheric hypoxia limits selection for large body size in insects. The result links ancient oxygen swings to the giants and dwarfs of insect history.
plos-pone-0003976: In 2008, Foerstner, Doerks, and Muller found a factory enzyme in a humble eukaryote. The single-celled choanoflagellate Monosiga brevicollis carried a working nitrile hydratase gene. Nitrile hydratases are prized catalysts for green industry and wastewater cleanup work. Finding one in a eukaryote widens the hunt for new natural helpers.
plos-pone-0004076: In 2008, Freire, Vilela, and Deus mined the first cancer genome atlas. They surveyed copy number alterations in glioblastoma multiforme. The Cancer Genome Atlas pilot set the template for big tumor catalogs. The survey maps gains and losses across a deadly brain cancer.
plos-pone-0004176: In 2009, Tuvim, Evans, and Clement found inflammation saving lungs. Boosted lung inflammation protected mice against influenza A pneumonia. The extra immune fire beat back the virus. The paradox reframes inflammation as a tunable defense. The result suggests priming lungs before flu season.
plos-pone-0004276: In 2009, Sakamoto, Matsuda, and Zuloaga linked stress to bedroom trouble. Stress disrupted a gastrin-releasing peptide circuit in the spinal cord. The circuit governs sexual function in male rats. The finding points beyond talk therapy. The spinal system offers a drug target for stress-linked dysfunction.
plos-pone-0358476: Measuring muscle fiber size under the microscope is slow, manual work. This paper shows that a web-based combination of Cellpose and SAM — two AI image-segmentation tools — can automatically outline muscle fibers in stained tissue sections. The automated measurements match manual ones, opening the door to much larger muscle studies.
plos-pone-0357776: Preparing DNA libraries for cancer sequencing is slow and fiddly work. This paper introduced OS-MPCR, a novel one-step multiplex PCR method for efficient NGS library preparation in cancer. The streamlined method cuts time and cost from the sequencing pipeline, getting answers to oncologists faster.
plos-pone-0357176: GPS tracks how far young soccer players run; heart rate reveals what it costs them. This study examined within-player associations between GPS-derived external training load and heart rate-based internal load in elite youth male soccer. The links help coaches calibrate training to each player’s actual strain.
plos-pone-0358176: Two metal-driven cell death pathways — ferroptosis (iron) and cuproptosis (copper) — may converge in rheumatoid arthritis. This integrative network analysis identified candidate genes shared between the pathways in RA pathogenesis. The shared genes become fresh therapeutic suspects for a disease that still defeats many drugs.
plos-pone-0357476: Americans’ relationship with science is multidimensional — and badly strained. This paper asked whether citizen science offers a path forward for rebuilding it. The findings explore whether participating directly in research restores public trust in science better than expert messaging ever could.
plos-pone-0357976: Mercury resistance genes flow through people, food, and water worldwide. This comparative study measured the prevalence of the merA resistance gene in human feces, food, and environmental water across Japan, Vietnam, and Ghana. The three-country comparison tracks how mercury resistance spreads through entire ecosystems.
plos-pone-0357276: Splicing introns out of RNA requires exquisite helicase choreography. This paper showed the G-patch protein Cwf28 interacts with the RNA helicase Cdc28 in catalytically active spliceosomes of fission yeast. The interaction clarifies a key step in how cells edit their genetic messages.
plos-pone-0357376: Orange peel waste holds valuable soluble dietary fiber — if you can extract it well. This paper valorized the by-product via ultrasound-pretreated enzymatic extraction, with full structural and functional characterization of the fiber. The work turns juice-industry trash into a functional food ingredient.
plos-pone-0356876: The type of cropland shapes the beneficial fungi living beneath it. This Ethiopian study showed cropland type shapes arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi population density and species diversity in the northwest. The findings guide farming practices that nurture — rather than destroy — these vital underground allies.
plos-pone-0356776: Nairobi’s wet markets feed millions — and their poultry vendors shape food safety daily. This paper studied the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of those vendors regarding food safety dynamics. The findings pinpoint where training and infrastructure would most reduce the risk on shoppers’ plates.
plos-pone-0352276: A year after breaking the shoulder’s top bone, elderly patients’ real-world activity tells the recovery story. This paper — drawing on two randomized trials — associated patient-reported outcomes with accelerometer-measured activity 12 months after proximal humerus fracture. The objective data validate what patients report about their healing.
plos-pone-0354976: Brain-computer interfaces that read motor imagery could be faster with smarter compression. This paper improved motor imagery BCI performance via task-unaware compression in the BELT Bayesian edge-cloud architecture. The compression scheme preserves the neural signals that matter while slashing bandwidth.
plos-pone-0356376: Predicting where a moving target will be next is critical for defense and air traffic alike. This research enhanced LSTM-based spatial target trajectory forecasting with attention mechanisms. The attention-boosted network focuses on the trajectory segments that matter most, sharpening predictions.
plos-pone-0356476: ‘I just don’t want to take up people’s time’ — that reluctance silences patients about their medications. This qualitative study explored psychological safety during patient–provider conversations about medicines. The intimate accounts reveal how power dynamics shut down questions — and how clinicians can invite the honesty that prevents harm.
plos-pone-0355376: Multiple sclerosis patients need rehabilitation that reaches them at home. This paper published the protocol for a pilot effectiveness and feasibility randomized controlled trial of an advanced telerehabilitation system for people with MS — the PLATFORM trial. The planned trial will test whether sophisticated remote rehab can genuinely improve function for patients who can’t easily reach clinics, potentially transforming MS care delivery.
plos-pone-0350376: Oncology trial submissions to regulators contain contradictions that humans miss. CAVE-Onc is a graph-constrained agentic AI system for validating cross-domain contradictions in CDISC oncology submissions. The agentic validation catches inconsistencies that could delay life-saving drug approvals.
plos-pone-0354676: Chemotherapy-induced hair loss devastates breast cancer patients — and scalp cooling might prevent it. The ICELAND protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial comparing scalp cooling against standard cold caps. The planned trial will determine which cooling approach genuinely saves patients’ hair — and dignity.
plos-pone-0355276: Surgical skill assessment needs validated performance indicators. This paper validated expected objective performance indicators in surgical data analysis. The validated metrics bring objectivity to judging surgical competence — with implications for training and credentialing.
plos-pone-0355676: Depressed adolescents might benefit from brain stimulation guided by their own connectivity maps. This paper tested the feasibility, safety, and preliminary efficacy of resting-state fMRI-guided rTMS for adolescents with major depressive disorder. The personalized neuromodulation approach brings precision psychiatry to young patients with few options.
plos-pone-0355476: AI might triage the flood of clinical referral letters — but the evidence needs systematic review. This paper published the protocol for reviewing AI models for referral interpretation and triage to acute and specialist care. The planned synthesis will separate the triage tools that work from the hype.
europmc-pmc2841576: How antioxidant-rich is your diet? This 2010 paper measures the total antioxidant content of more than 3100 foods, beverages, spices, herbs, and supplements used worldwide. The authors built one of the largest food antioxidant databases ever. The reference lets researchers and consumers compare foods on a common scale.
europmc-pmc2848976: A drug designed to block mutant BRAF in melanoma had an alarming side effect. This 2010 paper shows the inhibitor PLX4032 paradoxically activates the ERK pathway and boosts migration and proliferation in some melanoma cells. The authors document the backfire in detail. The finding warned that targeted drugs can help the wrong cells.
europmc-pmc2871176: The diabetes drug liraglutide mimics a gut hormone, and this 2009 trial tests it as an add-on. The authors report 26 weeks of liraglutide with a sulphonylurea beat the sulphonylurea alone for blood sugar and weight. Their trial backed a new drug class. The result helped launch GLP-1 drugs to prominence.
europmc-pmc2887476: A fungus's shape can decide its fate in the body. This 2010 paper shows cryptococcal cell size and shape affect how host cells engage it and how deadly it becomes. The authors link morphology to virulence. Their work explains why one strain kills and another does not.
europmc-pmc2924276: Bug taste and smell have deep roots. This 2010 paper traces insect scent receptors back to an ancient worm-like forebear. The authors follow how taste and smell gear evolved in insects. Their deep history rewrites the senses' family tree. The receptors still guide pest-control research today.
europmc-pmc2928176: Silver nanoparticles promise germ-killing socks and sprays, but safety data lagged. This 2010 rat study feeds rats silver nanoparticles for weeks and tracks the harm. The authors chart where damage lands. Their data informed safe limits for consumer goods. The study set a marker for nano-safety rules.
europmc-pmc2944076: Dirty air kills millions early, and this 2010 paper puts a number on it. The authors estimate the global burden of man-made ozone and fine particles on premature human mortality using atmospheric modeling. Their count spans the planet. The estimate powered pollution policy debates.
europmc-pmc3012676: Gene-switch arrays need the right math. This 2010 paper compares two ways to score methylation from chip data. The authors' bake-off guides analysts. Their work became a methods reference. The winner depends on the study design. Core labs still cite the verdict.
europmc-pmc3022776: Fly guts rebuild after infection with growth-signal help. This 2010 paper shows the fruit fly EGFR path steers stem cell growth and gut repair after germs strike. The authors reveal the repair crew. Their work lights up regeneration biology. Human guts likely use the same playbook.
europmc-pmc3053476: Quinolones moonlight as bacterial chatter. This 2011 review shows these antibiotic molecules also serve as germ-to-germ signals. The authors reveal the double life. Their overview aids anti-germ drugs. Pseudomonas eavesdrops on its own chatter. Jamming the signals disarms without killing.
europmc-pmc3084176: Bed nets pushed malaria mosquitoes outdoors. This 2011 Tanzania study finds surviving mosquitoes bite more outdoors after net campaigns. The authors reveal the shift. Their work demands new strategies. Indoor spraying misses the outdoor biters. New traps target the evening porch crowd.
europmc-pmc6566176: Protein-protein interactions run the cell, and blocking the bad ones is a prime drug strategy - but small molecules often cannot grip the flat interfaces. Peptides, the middle ground between small drugs and antibodies, can. This review surveys modern peptide drug design: how chemists stabilize these chains and where peptide medicines are winning.
europmc-pmc6629176: After a heart attack, the heart scars instead of regrowing - but circular RNAs may hold a key. Researchers found that silencing circRNA Nfix, controlled by a super-enhancer, unlocked heart-muscle regrowth in mice after infarction. The finding nominates a new RNA target for coaxing human hearts to heal.
europmc-pmc6659376: Mendelian randomization uses genes as nature's randomized trials to test causality - but the math leans on a shaky assumption called NOME. This paper improves two-sample summary-data MR by moving beyond it, giving epidemiologists sturdier causal estimates from genetic data. Better plumbing for a popular method.
europmc-pmc6669976: Catching cancer early may come down to reading tumor DNA floating in blood. This review covers next-generation sequencing in liquid biopsy: how NGS fishes circulating tumor DNA from a blood draw for screening. Cheaper, sharper sequencing is bringing early detection within reach.
europmc-pmc6701376: Designing health programs is harder than it looks - good intentions flop without method. This guidance distills a consensus exercise into principles and actions for building complex interventions. Researchers get a practical checklist for the messy work between idea and trial.
europmc-pmc6724476: Gold nanoparticles can turn light into heat - a trick with medical promise. This review covers plasmonic photothermal particles: how metallic nanoparticles absorb light and cook their surroundings. The controlled burn could target tumors or infections with surgical precision.
europmc-pmc6773876: Gene lists are boring - pathways tell stories. pathfindR is an R package that finds enriched pathways in omics data by walking protein interaction networks, not just counting genes. The active-subnetwork approach yields richer, more honest biological conclusions.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-76: GAO's 2007 report takes apart the FAA's math for billing airlines for air-traffic control. Much of the method passed muster, GAO found, but some key guesses and steps did not. The findings feed a never-ending air-policy brawl: who foots the bill for the skies, and whether the split is fair to the flyers paying it.
gao-gaoreports-b-299576: Meeks Disposal Corporation doubled its June 2007 protest — two case numbers, one trash-hauling fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm challenged the awards; the call weighs each claim. Garbage contracts, the ruling shows, get first-class bid law.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-276: Lejeune's poisoned water got a second GAO look in 2007 — the report details the follow-up on the Marine base's contamination legacy. The findings keep the official record straight. The report stands as the paper trail for families still seeking answers decades later.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-376: The Army's future war machines faced their moment of truth in 2007, and GAO's report says the key decisions on the Future Combat System could not wait. The findings frame the fork in the road. The report's warning: decide with data, or pay in sunk billions.
gao-gaoreports-b-299076: Fantastic Data came back for more in February 2007 — a second protest and a second ruling in the same month. The firm challenged another award, and the call tests these claims too. Repeat filers get repeat fairness, case by case. The second bite got the same fair look.
openalex-w7207777076: How do you grade a four-year-old fairly? This article studies how Brazilian policy documents instruct early-childhood educators to assess children, and it questions those instructions through a Foucauldian lens of power, knowledge, and norms. The qualitative document analysis asks whether official guidance ends up sorting children into normal and abnormal. A provocative piece that treats preschool assessment as a question of justice, not just technique.
openalex-w7205001176: When students act out, schools often treat boys and girls differently without realizing it. This article studies indiscipline and parent participation through the lens of gender, asking how families handle transgressions by sons versus daughters. The authors unpack the expectations baked into those responses. A thought-provoking look at how gender shapes the everyday discipline triangle of student, school, and family.
openalex-w7204229376: Jawbone cancer is rare, aggressive, and hard to diagnose early. This paper reviews progress on molecular markers for maxillofacial osteosarcoma: biological flags that could catch the tumor sooner and guide treatment. The authors survey recent advances. A specialized oncology review where a better test could mean a saved face, literally.
openalex-w7204179076: School principals live between spreadsheets and classrooms. This study looks at how school leaders balance administrative demands with teaching quality, and what leadership plus autonomy really require. The authors probe the tension between managing and inspiring. A management-education study of the person holding the whole school together.
openalex-w4411165576: Even diamonds go soft in the deep cold. This lab paper reports sound-wave tests showing lab-grown diamonds losing stiffness below 1 kelvin, near absolute zero. The team tested clear and yellow synthetic stones. A deep-freeze study of the hardest known stuff turning oddly floppy.
openalex-w4416229476: Enfortumab vedotin fights advanced bladder cancer but can ravage the skin. This analysis of phase trial data asks whether body mass index predicts who suffers side effects. The authors linked BMI trends to adverse events. A clinical study helping doctors dose smarter and warn the right patients.
openalex-w7166542376: A traveler landed in an ER vomiting nonstop after heavy weed use. This case report covers suspected CHS, a gut revolt in long-term cannabis users. The team traced the diagnosis step by step. A clinical story of a little-known weed hazard.
pmc-13467476: This 2026 immunology review covers the two-way chemical signaling between lung cancer cells and CD8+ T cells — the immune system's killer cells — mediated by microRNAs. pmc-13594676: This 2026 surgical paper reports a large case series on minimally invasive, tissue-preserving breast augmentation, sharing the technique and practical surgical pearls. By preserving native tissue rather than disrupting it, the approach aims for safer, more natural results. The detailed write-up lets other plastic surgeons learn from the authors' experience.
pmc-13429276: In this 2026 biomechanics study, healthy adults walked in shoes of mismatched length while researchers measured gait speed and lower-limb joint motion. Even small mismatches changed how people moved. The result is a reminder that footwear fit is a real biomechanical variable, not just comfort.
pmc-13351476: This 2026 qualitative study explored the nutritional health of the UK food manufacturing workforce through employees' own insights. The people who make food face distinct dietary pressures. The employee perspectives point to workplace interventions that could actually work.
pmc-13429876: A 2026 study performing deep immune profiling of endometrial and peripheral blood cells in endometriosis. Comparing immune cells at the disease site versus in circulation reveals what is local and what is systemic. The detailed profiles could yield biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
pmc-13559576: This 2026 multicenter cohort study linked the systemic immune-inflammation index to overall survival in leukemia patients. A simple blood-based index predicted outcomes. The finding supports its use in risk stratification.
pmc-13468076: A 2026 chemistry paper on triphenylamine-based supramolecular coordination metallacycles. The self-assembled rings have optoelectronic promise. The synthesis is the achievement.
pmc-13524876: In this 2026 review, sterol flux rewiring framed cholesterol biosynthesis as a dynamic signaling network. Cholesterol synthesis isn't just plumbing — it signals. The network view is the reframe.
pmc-13580676: This 2026 paper showed trichostatin A inhibited cytokines released in LPS-induced THP-1 cells by downregulating deacetylated syntaxin 17 and promoting autophagosome-lysosome fusion. The HDAC inhibitor's anti-inflammatory route was detailed. The mechanism is the contribution.
pmc-13529176: This 2026 review covered research developments in nanobiomaterials for tumor vaccines. Nanoparticles as vaccine platforms are advancing. The review surveys the developments.
pmc-13512776: This 2026 medicinal chemistry paper showed sulfonylurea bioisosteres of sulfonic acid in JFD 00458-based ST6GAL1 inhibitors enhanced membrane permeability. The swap improved drug-likeness. The bioisosteres are the design win.
pmc-13502776: A 2026 case report of durable response to olaparib plus continued PD-1 blockade in PALB2-mutated triple-negative breast cancer with leptomeningeal metastasis. The combination conquered the brain lining spread. The durable response is the hope.
